name: TX-26
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent running with no outside opposition spending
model.rationale: Brandon Gill is an incumbent in an R+11 district with a huge financial edge and no Democratic air support, while challenger Steven Shook has raised almost nothing; markets price his win at 98%. The fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold, so the forecast sits at a double-digit GOP margin.
model.watch: A late wave of Democratic outside spending or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, though a seat flip remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brandon Gill, the Republican incumbent, is seeking a second term in a north Texas district that leans about eleven points Republican. He has raised more than $4.2 million and holds $1.4 million on hand, while Democratic challenger Steven Shook has raised under $18,000. No outside groups are spending against Gill, and no expert raters list the race as competitive.

Prediction markets give Gill roughly a 98 percent chance of winning, and there are no public general-election polls to suggest the race is close. With a Libertarian also on the ballot, the expected outcome is a decisive Republican victory by roughly sixteen points.
